Song 'Aimo O.C.' is not in the glossary (only 'Aimo'). (Vocal) as in the sound-test rows.
tm kept; 2 px over the estimated box, same shape as u3418/u3419.
Same short form as u3396 (F Movie = Macross Frontier movie).
Parallels 'Macross 7: Prologue' (u3410), which is also a few px over its estimated box.

rows.en:
A rookie operator who makes up for inexperience with natural
cheer and hard work. Her looks and manner make people think
she's younger, which bothers her a lot. (CV: Kimiko Koyama)

A big-sister operator whose precise orders can be gentle or
strict. A bit pushy at times, but she looks after others, and
the crew adore her as a big sister. (CV: Tomo Adachi)

A prodigy operator whose talent was recognized while young.
She hates being treated like a child and always strives to be
an equal. A bit foul-mouthed, but endearing. (CV: Ai Nonaka)

A skilled operator who judges calmly. His harsh words get him
misunderstood; he's just bad at showing emotion and is warm
at heart. Glasses are his trademark. (CV: Kiyotaka Furushima)
An elite U.N. Forces officer, chief combat controller of the Macross air wing. A stiff, duty-first type Hikaru treated like an "old lady," she slowly falls for him. (CV: Mika Doi)
rows.notes: Misa Hayase (operator). Subject of the last clause is Misa: she grows fond of Hikaru.

rows.en: A lieutenant from the New U.N. Forces General Staff, sent to S.M.S. as an observer. Through the battles with the Vajra, she gradually gets back together with her ex, Ozma. (CV: Sanae Kobayashi)
Macross 7 fleet staff officer, whose vast knowledge made him a key aide. With Captain Max away, he helmed the Battle 7 as acting captain, showing superb skill. (CV: Ryusuke Obayashi)

VF-0 Ghost Booster
All-out assault spec using Ghosts as boosters.

VF-0 Reactive Armor
Add-on armor with missiles mounted all over.

SV-51 Twin Booster
Decisive-battle spec fitted with 2 jet boosters.

VF-1 Super Pack (TV)
Booster units enhance firepower and thrust.

VF-1 Super Pack (Movie)
The Valkyrie's standard gear for space.

VF-1 Strike Pack
Strike gear only leaders' units may carry.

VF-1 Armored Pack
Add-on armor with missiles mounted all over.

VF-11B FAST Pack
Booster units enhance firepower and thrust.

YF-19/VF-19A FAST Pack
A compact FAST Pack designed for stealth.

YF-21/VF-22 FAST Pack
A compact FAST Pack designed for stealth.

VF-11C FAST Pack
Booster units enhance firepower and thrust.

VF-11 Full Armored
Add-on armor with missiles mounted all over.

VF-11MAXL Kai Sound Booster
Fires sound beams powered by Song Energy.

VF-17T Kai Sound Booster
Fires sound beams powered by Song Energy.

VF-19 Kai Sound Booster
Fires sound beams powered by Song Energy.

VF-17 Super Pack
Gear with weapons upgraded to fight the Protodeviln.

VF-19 Atmosphere/Space Booster
Gear that works both in and out of the atmosphere.
rows.notes: Booster name is a plain translation (no glossary entry); description shared with u3454.

rows.en:
VF-25 Super Pack
The Messiah's standard gear for space.

VF-25 Super Pack
Klan wears the Super Pack herself.
rows.notes: Klan's giant form fitted with the VF-25 Super Pack.

rows.en:
VF-25 Armored Pack
Armored gear that transforms to all 3 modes.

VF-25 Tornado Pack
Gear that works both in and out of the atmosphere.

Armored Pack (Final Battle Spec)
Final-battle spec: Armored plus a sniper rifle.

VF-25 Fold Speaker
A speaker that amplifies the effects of song.

VF-171EX Armored Pack
Armored gear loaded with anti-Vajra weapons.

VF-2SS Super Armed Pack
SAP: the Valkyrie II's standard equipment.

SNN Valkyrie Large Booster
A large booster for the SNN Valkyrie.

U.N. Forces pilot. Shot down by Nora, he washes up on Mayan
Island and meets Sara. They clash, but slowly bond.
A fool who'd risk his life for a woman. (CV: Kenichi Suzumura)

U.N. Forces ace. A tough survivor of the Unification Wars and
a drinker whose motto is "Fear booze? Then you can't fight!"
Above all, a man who loves the open sky. (CV: Akira Kamiya)

Priestess of Mayan Island, Guide of the Wind. Overly hostile
to outsiders, she's hard on Shin too. But in the fight for AFOS
fragments, she slowly bonds with him. (CV: Sanae Kobayashi)
An Anti-U.N. Forces pilot whose family the U.N. Forces killed. Good enough to down Shin twice, she teamed with Ivanov to run rings around the U.N. Forces. (CV: Minami Takayama)

Anti-U.N. Forces ace pilot and Focker's former instructor.
Known as "Daisy Ivanov," he flies well enough to treat Focker
as a mere fledgling. (CV: Ryuzaburo Otomo)

A civilian pilot. Meeting Lynn Minmay, caught in a Zentradi
attack, he becomes a military pilot to protect her. Indecisive,
he wavers between two women. (CV: Kenji Nojima)

A veteran of the Unification Wars, as strong with drink and
women as in combat. Hikaru's senior, adored as a big brother.
Skull Squadron's leader and trusty ace. (CV: Akira Kamiya)

A pilot who shone from his very first sortie. Nickname: Max.
He beats the enemy ace Milia in battle, and this leads to him
later marrying the alien Milia. A rare talent. (CV: Sho Hayami)

Ex-Zentradi pilot. She sneaked into the Macross to find the
one who shot her down. She found Max, dueled him and lost.
He then proposed, and they married. (CV: Eri Takeda)

Hikaru's subordinate, a big, happy-go-lucky guy. His jokes
in battle get him in trouble; Hikaru or Max save him. A cheery,
easygoing goof, hard to hate. Avg. skill. (CV: Katsumi Suzuki)

Poster girl of Chinese diner Nyan-Nyan, she won Miss Macross
and became a top idol. Free-spirited, she toyed with Hikaru's
tender crush to her heart's content. (CV: Mari Iijima)

The top idol of the Macross. Through the "Minmay Attack," she
caused a culture shock that ended the interstellar war. A
legendary diva remembered for generations. (CV: Mari Iijima)

Zentradi division commander. Warlike and hotheaded, he rides
out front himself, bent on sinking the Macross. While many
chose to live with Earth, he sought battle. (CV: Kosuke Meguro)
A Meltrandi pilot. Known as "Milia the Ace," she was a crack pilot feared even by Zentradi soldiers. After losing her fight with Max, she marries him. (CV: Eri Takeda)

U.N. Forces pilot Maximilian Jenius in macronized form. To
cover the Macross in the final battle with the Boddole Zer Main
Fleet, he flew a Queadluun-Rau with Milia. (CV: Sho Hayami)

Giants created by the ancient Protoculture through genetic
engineering. Bred as combatants, they never knew "Culture,"
and overreact when they first encounter it.

Zentradi fleet commander. A master strategist, he corners the
Macross again and again. Touched by forbidden Culture in that
fight, he opts to coexist with Earth. (CV: Ryuzaburo Otomo)

Zentradi fleet commander. Contact with Culture awakened the
Culture asleep within him. In the final battle he turned on
Boddole Zer to fight for the Macross. (CV: Ryuzaburo Otomo)

Zentradi Main Fleet Supreme Commander. Fearing a myth that
Protoculture contact saps the will to fight, he deems cultured
humans Protoculture, to be destroyed. (CV: Osamu Ichikawa)

Zentradi Main Fleet Supreme Commander, and the central
bio-unit of his flagship. He grasps a little of Culture, and will
use any means, however cruel, to win. (CV: Osamu Ichikawa)

Chosen as a new fighter's test pilot for his superb flying skill.
He grew up with Myung and Guld but cut ties after an incident.
Dalmatian High School's wild child. (CV: Takumi Yamazaki)

Chief developer of the YF-21, a BDI-system prototype, and its
pilot too. He clashes hard with Isamu over the next-gen fighter
race and childhood friend Myung. (CV: Unsho Ishizuka)
Sharon's producer. Once childhood friends with Isamu and Guld, she cut ties after an incident. Reunited with them on Eden after 7 years, she is torn between the two. (CV: Rika Fukami)
rows.notes: tm fixed: 'on Eden 7 years later' read like a place called 'Eden 7'.

rows.en:
A virtual idol who became the galaxy's No. 1 right after debut.
With songs that have a hypnotic effect, she controls people
and plunges Macross City into chaos.
"My profile? You shouldn't go digging into people's pasts. Forget that and listen to my song! Wanna know about me? Listen to my song and you'll get it. Here we go!" (CV: Nobutoshi Canna)
rows.notes: Basara speaking in his own voice; seiyuu romanized as in u3501.

rows.en:
FIRE BOMBER's new vocalist. Max and Milia's child, she has
flown Valkyries since she was little, so she's a fine pilot too.
At an age where two boys are on her mind. (CV: Tomo Sakurai)

An elite pilot who joined special assault unit Diamond Force
young. He saw Basara, who sings in battle, as an enemy, but in
time trusts him and the power of song. (CV: Takehito Koyasu)

For his service in the Zentradi war, he became commander of
the Macross 7 colony fleet. Though retired, his genius piloting
is intact, and he flew Valkyries in ops. (CV: Sho Hayami)

City 7's mayor and a former Zentradi ace pilot. She still sorties
when City 7 is attacked, and citizens back her as their fighting
mayor. (CV: Eri Takeda)

Leader of FIRE BOMBER. A former U.N. Forces ace, he left the
military after an incident. Always backing Basara and Mylene,
he claims he's 28, which is doubtful. (CV: Masashi Sugawara)

FIRE BOMBER's drummer. Taciturn, she rarely speaks, and
mostly communicates through her drums. A pure-blooded
Zentradi with extraordinary strength.

rows.notes: Same form as the prefilled u3470 ('Support-character Misa does not appear.').

rows.en:
As Varauta Army commander, he was to raid Macross 7 for
Spiritia, but he defies Gepelnitchi's orders to awaken one of
his comrades, "Sivil". (CV: Tomohiro Nishimura)

He took over the Varauta Army from Gigile and tormented the
Macross 7 fleet. He dubs all he sees some kind of "Beauty". He
can fuse with Glavil into his ultimate form. (CV: Akio Suyama)

Varauta Army Supreme Commander, with the dread power to
drain all the galaxy's Spiritia. For his Spiritia Farm Project,
meant to give endless Spiritia, he relentlessly hunted Basara.

A Protodeviln girl. Drawn to Basara's song, she seeks him
out again and again. In the end she sings with him and evolves
into a self-regenerating Spiritia race. (CV: Akiko Nakagawa)

"The galaxy sure has some strange folks in it..." -- Graham
(CV: Nobutoshi Canna)

A taciturn man bent only on killing the white Galaxy Whale that
took his right arm and his wife. Oddly, he hit it off with Basara,
which surprised even his daughter Elma. (CV: Joji Nakata)

A sunny, innocent, slightly ditzy girl from planet Zola who
dreams of being a pro singer. How she makes it and her name
rings across the galaxy is a tale for later. (CV: Aya Sakaguchi)

A high schooler in pilot training who becomes a Valkyrie pilot
after a Vajra attack. Born to a famed kabuki line, his gift and
looks once had him play female roles. (CV: Yuichi Nakamura)

Alto's classmate, a crack sniper. Motto: "Enemies or women, I
bring down whatever I aim at." He and Klan go way back. His
older sister was also a soldier and sniper. (CV: Hiroshi Kamiya)

Alto's junior. An electronics whiz, he is also special adviser
to major firm L.A.I.'s tech research division. In battle he flies
the EW RVF-25, controlling drone fighters. (CV: Jun Fukuyama)

S.M.S. Pixie Team leader, flying a crimson Queadluun-Rhea.
In battle she's a giant Zentradi, but when micronized her body
turns into a little girl's. (CV: Megumi Toyoguchi)

S.M.S. Pixie Team leader. Micronized, a genetic anomaly
gives her a young girl's body, and oddly a childish personality.
Michel teases her; they always bicker. (CV: Megumi Toyoguchi)
An S.M.S. Skull Squadron pilot who serves as a medic when not in combat. A superb pilot, she flies the three-seat Konig Monster all by herself. (CV: Houko Kuwashima)
rows.notes: Canaria Berstein (female per glossary). Konig without umlaut (font).

rows.en: Helmsman of the Macross Quarter. He has a pure maiden's heart, but when he gets worked up in battle, rough macho talk may slip out... A maiden with a sweet crush on Ozma. (CV: Kenta Miyake)
rows.notes: Bobby Margot: male per glossary, speaks in feminine Japanese; the source calls him a maiden (otome), kept.

rows.en:
Captain of the Macross Quarter and the pillar of S.M.S.
A former pilot, reportedly as skilled as Ozma, with a broad
view that reads the tide of battle. (CV: Toru Okawa)

The Super Dimension Cinderella who met Alto & co. and ran up
the glorious stairway to idol stardom. Kira☆. Her love battle
with Sheryl over Alto has just begun. (CV: Megumi Nakajima)

A girl just starting up the stairway to idol stardom. Aiming for the top, she cosplays in all sorts of commercials. Apart from a song called "Aimo," her childhood memories are gone. (CV: Megumi Nakajima)
A diva hailed as the Galactic Fairy. Supremely confident in herself as Sheryl, she is extremely proud. Her love battle with Ranka over Alto has only just begun. (CV: Aya Endo)
A diva hailed as the Galactic Fairy. Close to Alto, whom she met on Frontier, she oddly knows the one song Ranka remembered, raising suspicion she's a Galaxy spy. (CV: Aya Endo)
rows.notes: 'Galaxy' = the Macross Galaxy fleet, as the Japanese says.

rows.en: Alto & co.'s classmate. A part-timer at Chinese diner Nyan-Nyan, she met Ranka there and feels more than friendship for her. Ranka Lee Fan Club founder and fan No. 1. (CV: Houko Kuwashima)

A cyborg pilot who blocked Alto time and again. Emotionless,
he saw his missions as his whole reason to exist, but through
his time with Ranka he slowly changes. (CV: Soichiro Hoshi)

Sheryl's formidable manager, but in truth the mastermind who
brought the Vajra to the Frontier fleet. She schemes to use the
power of Ranka and the Vajra to rule all. (CV: Kikuko Inoue)
An entertainment reporter for TV station SNN. Fighting the Mardook, he meets Silvie and Ishtar and awakens to a passion for bringing the truth to the people. (CV: Tsutomu Takayama)
Leader of the U.N. Forces' Faerie Squadron. A quarter Meltran, she inherited her grandmother's recklessness. She and Hibiki clash time and again, but slowly fall for each other. (CV: Yumi Toma)
rows.notes: Silvie Gena. 'Faerie Squadron' is a provisional glossary entry (the Japanese says Fairy Leader squadron).

rows.en:
An Emulator of the Mardook army. Taken by Hibiki, she met
Earth culture and learned what culture means. Through Ars's
song, she ended the Mardook war. (CV: Hiroko Kasahara)

Raised rich, he wanted for nothing, but bored of a life with no
thrills, he became a pilot. A seasoned veteran, foul-mouthed
but admired as a good big brother. (CV: Tetsu Inada)

Trained hard from childhood by her mercenary father, she's
a proven pilot. Perhaps as a single dad raised her, she's rough,
but has a feminine side: her hobby is cooking. (CV: Miho Hino)

A rookie who has dreamed of being a pilot since he was small.
Honest and earnest, with a slightly timid streak, but once his
blood is up, he shows a bold side. (CV: Jun Konno)

A passionate pilot who deeply loves the sky. His impulsiveness
lands him in all kinds of trouble, on and off the job. His hobby
is collecting oddly patterned T-shirts. (CV: Yuki Hayashi)

Born into a military family where all must serve, she became
a pilot, rare for a woman even there. Bright and friendly to all,
she often gives men the wrong idea. (CV: Hinako Sasaki)

An unlucky girl who enlisted hoping to be a mechanic, only to be made a pilot by her aptitude test. She is a quarter Zentradi, and her strong point is being full of pointless energy. (CV: Yoko Nishino)

rows.en:
EX-Gear Basics: Walk Mode
These instructions use the default
controller settings. Please keep this in mind.
rows.notes: Same three-line shape for every EX-Gear Basics header (u3551, u3559, u3564, u3567, u3574, u3575, u3582).

rows.en:
Push the analog stick down
to switch to Walk mode.

Press Up, Down, Left or Right on the D-pad
to move forward, back, left or right.
rows.notes: Same wording as the prefilled u3618 (same Japanese).

rows.en:
Quickly press the D-pad twice in the same
direction to step that way.
Keep holding the D-pad to dash.

Keep holding the × button mid-jump
to float in the air.

Press the D-pad while floating
to move through the air, too.
You can dash even in mid-jump.

Practice the Walk mode controls.
Leaving the room ends the training.

You can lock on to the red rings
by pressing the R button.

Press the L button to point the camera
in the direction of travel.

EX-Gear Basics: Hover Mode
These instructions use the default
controller settings. Please keep this in mind.

Push the analog stick left or right
to switch to Hover mode.

Press Left or Right on the D-pad to turn.
Press the L button to stop in place.

Quickly press the D-pad twice
in the same direction to step
that way.

At the end of a step,
keep holding the D-pad to dash.

Hold the × button to boost upward
and gain altitude.

Quickly press the × button twice
and keep holding it to boost
downward and lose altitude.

Practice the Hover mode controls.
Leaving the room ends the training.

EX-Gear Basics: Flight Mode
These instructions use the default
controller settings. Please keep this in mind.

Push the analog stick up
to switch to Flight mode.

Press Left or Right on the D-pad to turn,
Up to nose down and descend,
and Down to nose up and climb.

Press the × button
to boost and speed up.
rows.notes: Trailing newline kept as in the Japanese.

rows.en:
Practice the Flight mode controls.
Leaving the room ends the training.

EX-Gear Basics: Flight Mode
These instructions use the default
controller settings. Please keep this in mind.
rows.notes: Japanese writes EX-Gear without the hyphen here; same English.

rows.en:
Press the × button to boost.
Hold the △ button to brake
and slow down.

Quickly press Up, Left or Right on the D-pad
twice in the same direction to roll
that way.

EX-Gear Basics: Shooting Attacks
These instructions use the default
controller settings. Please keep this in mind.

Quickly press and release the R button
to lock on to an enemy.

While locked on, quickly press and release
the R button again to switch your lock
to another enemy.

Hold Up on the D-pad while locking on
to switch your lock to enemy warships
or enemy aces.

Press the □ button to shoot the target
you're locked on to.

While the locked-on target is in front of you,
your hit rate goes up.

Practice the shooting attack controls.
Leaving the room ends the training.

EX-Gear Basics: Shooting Attacks
These instructions use the default
controller settings. Please keep this in mind.

EX-Gear Basics: Melee Attacks & Guard
These instructions use the default
controller settings. Please keep this in mind.

In Walk and Hover modes, press
the △ button for melee attacks.

Press the △ button repeatedly
to chain melee attacks.

Lock on to a target. The
closer you are to it, the easier
it is to land melee attacks.

In Walk mode, hold
the L button to guard.
Guarding reduces the damage you take.

To dodge incoming balls,
use a step or a dash; to block them,
your best bet is to guard.

Practice the melee attack controls.
Leaving the room ends the training.

EX-Gear Basics: Melee Attacks & Guard
These instructions use the default
controller settings. Please keep this in mind.

Set a container down
near the start point to finish retrieving it.

You can also lift containers
in Hover mode.

Move close to a locked-on switch
to open the door.

Press the R button to lock on
to switches and containers.

EX-Gear Basics: Supply Transport
These explanations assume the default
controller settings. Please keep this in mind.
rows.notes: Title line names the drill (basic EX-Gear controls: supply transport). EX-Gear modes rendered Walk / Hover / Flight mode.

rows.en:
Lock on to a container and move close
to it, and you can
pick it up.

Press the □ button to set
the container down where you are.

You can only carry containers
in Walk mode or Hover mode.

Also, be careful: you can't
attack while you're
carrying a container.

Lock on to a door switch and move close
to it, and you can
operate the switch.

Hold Down on the D-pad while locking on
to lock on to containers and
switches first.

Now practice transporting supplies.
Leaving the room ends the training.

EX-Gear Basics: Switching Modes
These explanations assume the default
controller settings. Please keep this in mind.

You can switch the EX-Gear's mode
with the analog stick.

Push the analog stick down for Walk mode,
left or right for Hover mode,
and up for Flight mode.

In every mode, you can move
your unit with the D-pad.

In Walk mode, press Up, Down, Left or Right
on the D-pad to move that way.
rows.notes: Japanese: Up/Down/Left/Right move forward/back/left/right; compressed to 'move that way' for width.

rows.en:
Now go ahead and begin your
mode-switching training.

Leaving this room
ends the training.

Force enemy surrender
(destroy only their mechs)
rows.notes: Mission objective: make enemy soldiers surrender (destroy only their machines). TM line was too wide; reworded.

rows.en: Let's go over the basics of Fighter mode.

During training, flight mode is set to
Normal Flight, and controller settings are
reset to defaults. Please keep this in mind.

Press Up on the D-pad to nose down and
descend, and Down to nose up and climb.
Press Left or Right on the D-pad to turn.

Hold the L button and press Left or Right
on the D-pad to yaw.
(Real Flight only)

Press the × button to boost.
You can keep boosting until the
boost gauge is full.

Quickly press Down on the D-pad twice
to fire reverse thrust and decelerate sharply.

Hold the △ button to
brake and slow down.

Push the analog stick up
to transform into Fighter mode.

That covers the basics of Fighter mode.
Note: in this training you can't transform
into any mode other than Fighter.

Now go ahead and begin your
Fighter mode flight training.

Training ends when you reach
the target area or time runs out.
Let's go over the basics of Battroid mode.

During training, the controller settings
are reset to their defaults.
Please keep this in mind.

Press Up, Down, Left or Right on the D-pad
to move forward, back, left or right.

At the end of a step, keep holding
the D-pad to dash.

Quickly press the × button twice
and keep holding it to boost downward
and lose altitude.

Push the analog stick down
to transform into Battroid mode.

That covers the basics of Battroid mode.
Note: in this training you can't transform
into any mode other than Battroid.

Now go ahead and begin your
Battroid mode training.
Let's go over the basics of GERWALK mode.
Press Left or Right on the D-pad to turn.

In GERWALK mode, you hold your altitude
and hover.

Quickly press the × button twice
and keep holding it to boost downward
and lose altitude.

Push the analog stick left or right
to transform into GERWALK mode.

That covers the basics of GERWALK mode.
Note: in this training you can't transform
into any other mode.
rows.notes: TM ended 'into any mode other than GERWALK'; shortened to 'any other mode' for the short third line.

rows.en:
Now go ahead and begin your
GERWALK mode training.
Let's go over shooting attack basics.

Hold Down on the D-pad while locking on
to switch your lock to containers
or switches.

While locked on, hold the L button
and quickly tap the R button
to release the lock-on.

Press the □ button to attack the locked-on
enemy with your main weapon.

Press the ○ button to attack the locked-on
enemy with your special weapon.

If your unit has several special weapons,
hold the L button and press the □ button
to switch between them.

Some special weapons are capable of
multi-lock-on, which locks on to
several enemies at once.

To multi-lock-on, hold the ○ button
to lock on to multiple enemies
within range.

Release the ○ button during multi-lock-on
to hit every enemy locked at that moment
with your special weapon.

While the locked-on enemy is ahead of you,
your lock-on level goes up.

Shooting with a raised lock-on level
gives you bonuses to attack power
and accuracy.

These shooting controls are the same
in Fighter, Battroid
and GERWALK modes.
Let's go over melee attack basics.

In GERWALK and Battroid modes,
press the △ button to make a melee attack.

The number of hits in a combo varies
by unit and mode.

The higher your pilot's melee stat,
the more hits your combos get.

Hold the △ button for a moment, then
release it to perform a
charged melee attack.

Press the △ button while dashing
to perform a dash melee attack.

In Battroid mode, chain melee attacks
while holding Down on the D-pad
to perform a launching melee attack.

A launched enemy is left defenseless
for a short time.
You can attack it further during that time.

In Battroid mode, press the △ button
to hit a downed enemy with a down attack.

Please note that Fighter mode
has no melee attacks.

In Fighter mode, while locked on,
hold the R button to turn
and bring the enemy dead ahead.

In Battroid mode, hold the L button
to guard.
Guarding reduces the damage you take.

Guarding while no enemy is locked on
resets the camera angle
to face forward.

While guarding, press Up, Left or Right
on the D-pad to move
without dropping your guard.

In GERWALK mode, hold the L button
to hover and hold
your position.

While hovering, press Left or Right on the
D-pad to strafe while facing forward.

You can also step left or right and dash
while strafing.

In Battroid or GERWALK mode, press the
× button right after taking a knockdown hit
to avoid getting knocked down.

And even if you do get knocked down,
mashing the × button lets you recover
from being down faster.

If you have a wingman, press the SELECT
button together with the D-pad
to issue tactical commands.

The D-pad left tactical command
orders your wingman to focus
on melee attacks.

The D-pad right tactical command
orders your wingman to focus
on shooting attacks.

The D-pad up tactical command
orders your wingman to focus
on defense.

The D-pad down tactical command
orders your wingman to unleash
a Special Attack.

Hold the L button and press the ○ button
to spend 1 block of the SP Gauge
and fire a Charge Shot.

Hold the L button and press the △ button
to spend 1 block of the SP Gauge
and perform a Charge Melee attack.

Please note that Charge Melee is
not available in Fighter mode.

Hold the L button and press the × button
to spend 1 block of the SP Gauge
and perform a Charge Boost.

In Fighter mode, a Charge Boost
hits like a melee attack.

In Battroid and GERWALK modes,
press the △ button during a Charge Boost
to perform a melee attack.

Press the △ and ○ buttons together
to spend 3 blocks of the SP Gauge
and unleash a powerful Special Attack.

Press the ○ and × buttons together
to spend a set number of blocks
and use a Command Skill.

Hold the L button and press the △ and
○ buttons together to perform a
Combo Special Attack with your wingman.

A Combo Special Attack uses
3 blocks of the SP Gauge.
Now I'll explain how to carry containers.

You can only carry containers
in GERWALK or Battroid mode.
That covers how to carry containers.

Training's over once you bring the container
to the designated point, reach the target
area, or run out of time.

Now I'll explain the basic Real Flight
controls for Fighter mode.

During training, flight mode is set to
Real Flight, and controller settings are
reset to defaults. Please keep this in mind.

Press Up on the D-pad to pitch down,
and Down on the D-pad to pitch up.
Press Left or Right on the D-pad to roll.

Hold the L button and press Left or Right
on the D-pad to yaw.

In Real Flight, hold the R button
while locked on to swing
the camera toward your target.
That covers the basic Real Flight controls.

All right, go ahead and practice
flying in Real Flight.

With your current option parts equipped,
the option part transformation limit means
you can't switch to Fighter on the ground.

Press the ○, △, □ and
× buttons at the same time
to purge your option parts.

In Fighter mode, with an enemy locked on,
hold the R button to turn
and bring the enemy dead ahead.

Fighter mode no longer has a Charge Melee.
Instead, it can now perform a Charge Boost
that hits like a melee attack.

Hold Up on the D-pad while locking on
to switch your lock to enemy aces
or disabled wingmen.

Lock on to a disabled wingman and
move close to bring them
back into action.
That covers the basics of Special Maneuvers 3.

Now I'll explain the
Anti-Missile Action.

Hold the × button and press the □ button
to shoot down enemy missiles with gunfire:
that's the Anti-Missile Action.

When you're targeted by an enemy missile,
a Missile Marker appears
on screen.

A yellow Missile Marker shows an enemy
missile that is outside the range
of your Anti-Missile Action.

Once the Missile Marker turns red,
you can shoot that enemy missile down.

You can shoot missiles down
in Battroid or GERWALK mode.

In Fighter mode, and on some units,
Anti-Missile Action scatters flares
to bring down enemy missiles.

That concludes the explanation of
Anti-Missile Action.

The targets will fire missiles at you,
so practice using
Anti-Missile Action.

Now I'll explain the newly added special
maneuvers and the special maneuvers
whose controls have been updated.

With SP Gauge to spare,
hold the L and R buttons and press △
to unleash a Charge Break.
rows.notes: Game-system term 'Charge Break' (not in glossary). 'SP Gauge to spare' = Japanese 'when there is SP Gauge'.

rows.en:
During a Charge Break,
enemy attacks can't hurt you, but
you can't boost or attack either.
rows.notes: Japanese: you take no enemy attacks, in exchange you cannot boost or attack.

rows.en:
Once you unleash a Charge Break,
the SP Gauge itself is gone
for the rest of that mission.
rows.notes: Japanese: the SP Gauge itself disappears for that mission.

rows.en:
With a multi-lock weapon, hold the L button
and keep holding the ○ button
to lock on to a single target.
rows.notes: Japanese 'single lock' rendered as 'lock on to a single target'.

rows.en:
With a multi-lock weapon, while locked on,
keep holding the ○ button
to enter Plus Lock.

That covers the new special maneuvers
and those with updated controls.

If you missed an explanation,
you can hear it again anytime.
Make sure you learn the controls!

rows.en: July, A.D. 1999. The object that fell onto South Ataria Island, a lone Pacific isle,
was a giant space battleship, built with technology far beyond Earth's science.
The battleship brought a technological revolution through OverTechnology,
but it also pointed to an unknown threat from extraterrestrial life.
A.D. 2000. To counter the threat that was sure to come from space,
humanity founded the "U.N. Government," a body above all nations.
However, no small number of factions opposed it,
and they banded together as the Anti-U.N. Forces,
sparking the conflict that would later be called the "Unification Wars."
The war dragged on, finally ending in 2007. Meanwhile, the giant battleship
was under constant repair, to be reborn as a U.N. Forces battleship.
After so many years of war, the threat from space that had started it all
was all but forgotten. Yet the hour of destiny was close at hand...
A.D. 2040. In search of new places to live, humanity
had sent many large-scale colony fleets out into space.
Numerous planets had been discovered and developed into colony worlds,
and an age had come when many a generation called one of them home.
Drawn into the first interstellar war in history 30 years earlier,
humanity had narrowly escaped extinction by wielding the power of "Culture,"
rows.notes: TM had lowercase 'culture'; glossary term is 'Culture' (the Japanese puts it in brackets).

rows.en: made peace with the Zentradi forces, and founded the New U.N. Government.
But the end of the war did not simply mean the arrival of peace.
The work began with postwar reconstruction, then quelling some Zentradi remnants,
rows.notes: TM opened with a bare 'It' with no referent; made it 'The work'.

rows.en: and went as far as bolstering defenses against unknown threats yet to come.
The New U.N. Forces were still absolutely indispensable,
and the buildup of new fighting strength went on as well...
A.D. 2045. The 37th colony fleet, which had left Earth seven years earlier,
built around Macross 7, 7th of the New Macross class, with over a million citizens aboard,
rows.notes: TM moved 'over a million citizens' to the next row; the Japanese has it on this row, so the cut was moved back. 557 px of 560.

rows.en: was traveling through space in search of a new planet to settle.
The fleet's commander, who was also captain of the space carrier Battle 7,
was Maximilian Jenius, the genius pilot of Space War I.
Meanwhile, City 7, Macross 7's living area, had a mayor who even among the Zentradi
rows.notes: TM put 'governed by Mayor Milia' on this row; the Japanese names her and governs on the next row. Re-cut so this row ends at 'even among the Zentradi'.

rows.en: had once been feared as "Milia the Ace": Mayor Milia.
She was also Max's wife, wed to him in wartime in the first interstellar marriage.
Led by these two former aces, the Macross 7 fleet sailed on in peace,
but that a battle with the fearsome Varauta Army lay in wait for them
was something not a single person had foreseen...
A.D. 2059, 49 years after the end of humanity's first interstellar war.
The 25th giant colony fleet to set out, the "Macross Frontier,"
was sailing on toward the center of the galaxy.
The living areas inside the ship recreated the same environment as Earth's,
and over 10 million people went about their peaceful daily lives.
But at the end of that tranquil voyage,
a fierce battle against unknown space creatures lay in wait,
and almost none of the citizens had any idea...
The giant battleship that fell on South Ataria Island in the late 20th century
made humanity aware of extraterrestrial life and the threat it posed, while
it also brought about a technological revolution through OverTechnology.
But the impact the giant battleship had on Earth did not stop there.
the "U.N. Government" was founded, a body above all nations, while
factions around the world that rejected the U.N. Government's monopoly
on OverTechnology organized themselves into the "Anti-U.N. Forces."
The "U.N. Forces" and the "Anti-U.N. Forces." Their conflict grew fiercer
and at last sparked the struggle later called the "Unification Wars."
Amid the still-raging Unification Wars, on Mayan Island, a lone southern isle,
readings were picked up that, like the crashed battleship, seemed alien-made,
and the object giving them off was discovered.
Over this mysterious object, which must have been on Earth since antiquity,
the "U.N. Forces" and "Anti-U.N. Forces" began a secret but fierce struggle...
The battleship brought a technological revolution through OverTechnology,
but it also pointed to an unknown threat from extraterrestrial life.
To counter the threat that was sure to come from space,
the U.N. Government then repaired the giant battleship that crashed to Earth
and remade it as the U.N. Forces battleship "Macross."
As fate would have it, the threat from space came on the Macross's launch day.
Having sensed the Macross, an alien battleship appeared near Earth,
and hostilities with it suddenly broke out.
To escape the overwhelming enemy attack, the Macross risked a fold.
With 50,000 citizens aboard, it jumped to the outer solar system, near Uranus.
The Macross began its journey home to Earth,
but it could not shake off the relentless pursuit of the alien enemy.
And today, once again, the aliens launched their attack...
Zola, a planet on the edge of the Milky Way.
Home to the Zolans since ancient times, it was a quiet, utterly ordinary planet
where the Zolans lived easygoing, tranquil lives.
But Zola had one thing that set it apart.
Mysterious giant life-forms that at times appeared nearby: the "Galaxy Whales."
Long revered and feared as gods on Zola, the Galaxy Whales
were in fact thought to be energy beings with a plant-like structure.
But once it was known that the whales could power high-performance ships,
there was no end of poachers illegally hunting the whales for the black market,
and the Zolan Star Patrol, guarding the whales, struggled with armed poachers.
And now, once again this year, the season of the Galaxy Whales had come...
was sailing near the center of the galaxy.
rows.notes: Predicate only: the subject sits in the two lines before it, which reuse shared strings (very likely u3944/u3945: A.D. 2059 ... the 25th fleet, 'Macross Frontier,'). Written to follow 'the "Macross Frontier,"'.

rows.en: Inside the ships, an environment no different from Earth's had been artificially created,
and over 10 million people lived there, mainly on the residential ship...
rows.notes: Japanese: over 10 million lived, centered on the residential ship(s) (kyojuukan).

rows.en: The Macross Galaxy fleet was also sailing nearby,
and the two fleets, Galaxy and Frontier, kept close ties.
rows.notes: Japanese: (the Galaxy fleet) had mutual exchanges with the Frontier fleet.

rows.en: Then, from the Galaxy, came the diva known as the "Galactic Fairy,"
rows.notes: Sentence runs into u3997; Japanese is historical present ('comes to Frontier on a live tour'); rendered in past like the rest of the narration.

rows.en: "Sheryl Nome," bringing her concert tour to Frontier.
rows.notes: Sheryl's name is in brackets in the Japanese; kept as quotes.

rows.en: And it was from there that a new threat to humanity began to stir...
The battle for Earth's fate, between the U.N. Forces and the Boddole Zer Main Fleet,
rows.notes: Boddole Zer Main Fleet per organizations.json (bodoru kikan kantai).

rows.en: thanks to Lynn Minmay's song and the aid of Vrlitwhai's Adoclass fleet, which it moved,
rows.notes: Fleet name 'Adoclass' not in glossary (Japanese: Buritai Adokurasu kantai). Rendered "Vrlitwhai's Adoclass fleet".

rows.en: ended in a U.N. Forces victory. Earthlings and Zentradi made peace and chose to coexist.
In the years since, Earth faced alien threats time and time again,
but each time pulled through thanks to variable fighters and the power of song.
Time went by, and it was now A.D. 2090. The Macross that once saved Earth lay in ruin,
rows.notes: Japanese has seireki mid-line; A.D. kept since this is the era's establishing year.

rows.en: and humanity flourished alongside the micronized Zentradi.
But a new threat was steadily creeping up on humanity...
In an instant, the attack of the Boddole Zer Main Fleet left Earth in ruins.
Only one weapon could stand against the overwhelming might of the Zentradi:
If Zentradi soldiers, who had never known Culture, were made to hear a song,
rows.notes: TM had lowercase 'culture'; glossary term is 'Culture'.

rows.en: the shock would surely throw them into chaos.
Clinging to that faint hope, the Macross set out for the final battle.
Minmay's song was relayed by Vrlitwhai's flagship
to every ship in the Zentradi fleet.
Just as predicted, the Zentradi forces fell into chaos.
Staking humanity's fate, the Macross advanced on the heart of the enemy.
Its target: Supreme Commander Boddole Zer's flagship, the Fulbtzs-Berrentzs.
With Minmay's song ringing out, the Macross plunged into the enemy flagship.
Boddole Zer fell before the Macross's all-out attack.
Having lost their command at the center, the Zentradi
no longer had the strength to stand against the Macross and Vrlitwhai's fleet.
And with the battle over, the Macross returned to Earth.
Two races created by the Protoculture,
the people of Earth and the Zentradi.
With the end of the war, the two began to walk a single path together.
But the embers of conflict between them had not yet completely died out...
Quamzin, unable to accept Culture and refusing to coexist with Earth's people,
rows.notes: TM had lowercase 'culture'; glossary term is 'Culture'.

rows.en: turned peaceful Macross City into a battlefield.
But the Macross rose again, and its main cannon set Quamzin's ship ablaze,
and Quamzin and his crew vanished into the flames.
And so Quamzin's rebellion came to an end.
The Macross was badly damaged in this battle, but meanwhile, a new spaceship
was being built: a colony ship to seek a new world beyond the solar system.
To protect their Culture, humanity set out on a great journey across the galaxy...
At Macross City's ceremony marking 30 years since the end of Space War I,
Sharon Apple, who had already become self-aware,
hacked into the Macross's main computer
and seized control of Macross City's entire information network.
She even went so far as to put the people of the whole city under mind control.
Meanwhile, two fighters were heading for Macross City.
They were the YF-19 and YF-21, prototypes whose development was frozen.
Sharon tried to destroy them with the X-9 Ghost drone and the Macross, but
thanks to their machines' astonishing power and the pilots' desperate stand,
the core of the information network was destroyed. Sharon was dead.
And so the Macross's rampage under Sharon Apple was brought to a halt.
The incident was classified top secret, known only to a few insiders, but
it brought the danger of rogue unmanned fighters and artificial intelligence
to light as a serious problem.
In the end, the full-scale introduction of the Ghost was shelved,
and along with that, the development of manned fighters was resumed.
The nearly derailed development competition ended in victory for the YF-19,
which was officially adopted as the VF-19 Excalibur.
Meanwhile, the losing YF-21's capabilities were also highly rated,
and it was later given its chance to shine as the high-performance VF-22.
And so, at the same time and in the same place, two legendary machines were born.
rows.notes: meiki = celebrated machines (the VF-19 and VF-22).

rows.en: The war against the Protodeviln, led by the immensely powerful Gepelnitchi,
Just as in Space War I,
it was the power of the songs of Basara Nekki and friends that ended the war.
Once able to survive only by absorbing the Spiritia of other living things,
the Protodeviln, by singing together with Basara,
evolved into a race able to produce Spiritia on their own.
And so, with no more need to steal Spiritia, the Protodeviln
departed for some unknown, faraway corner of space.
Afterwards, Basara went on to make his mark as the vocalist of Fire Bomber
and became a singer whose voice thundered across the galaxy.
Yet the man himself had no interest whatsoever in such fame,
and he would end up wandering space alone. But that is another story.
Meanwhile, though the Macross 7 fleet had lost Battle 7,
it journeyed on through space, once again in search of a new planet to settle.
Searching for a place, somewhere out there, to call home for good...
rows.notes: Fragment after a full stop, as in the Japanese ('seeking a place of permanent settlement somewhere...').

rows.en: The giant Ranka was an illusion draped over
the Battle Galaxy, which had been placed under Grace's control.
Ranka, who had been held captive inside the Galaxy,
regained consciousness thanks to Sheryl's song and Alto's voice.
But now it was Sheryl, her strength spent, who collapsed.
Alto and Ranka called out to Sheryl, trying to rouse her.
Recognized by the Vajra through Ranka, Sheryl
was at last freed from the grip of the V-type virus.
Sheryl and Ranka sang, each striving to outdo the other.
Their song gave strength to a renewed counterattack against Grace.
What's more, the power of Ranka and Sheryl's songs
even freed the Vajra that Grace had held under her control.
The Vajra and humanity formed a united front and stood against Grace.
Faced with that power, Grace was no longer any match for them.
Grace's ambition to rule the galaxy by exploiting both the Vajra and humanity
Their battle over, the Frontier fleet set down on the Vajra homeworld.
Humanity and the Vajra: utterly different life-forms that never got along.
And yet it turned out they could understand one another.
And so a new world was born, where the Vajra and humanity live side by side...
Revived after absorbing Sara, the Bird Human used its overwhelming might
to wreak utter destruction, bent on wiping out a humanity that kept fighting.
In that hopeless situation, Shin's voice managed to awaken Sara's heart.
But Operation Iconoclasm had already been set in motion.
Reaction weapons flew to destroy the Bird Human, deemed uncontrollable.
To protect Earth, Mayan Island, and above all Shin, Sara flew off into space,
taking with her the reaction weapons she had sealed away with her own power.
Thus both ruin by the Bird Human and reaction-weapon fallout were averted.
But Shin's fighter had lost all control and was simply plummeting.
His ejection system had failed too, leaving him no way to escape.
Shin's fighter, which seemed certain to crash,
began to climb, wrapped in a mysterious light,
as the people of Mayan Island looked on,
rows.notes: Mid-sentence: Shin's fighter began to climb ... as the people of Mayan Island watched ... as if chasing Sara.

rows.en: as if chasing after Sara, who had vanished into space...
Before the enemy's overwhelming strength, the Macross seemed helpless.
But then, an unexpected ally appeared.
Moved by Minmay's song, Vrlitwhai and a faction of the Zentradi forces
had risen in revolt against Boddole Zer.
Refusing to let humanity be wiped out and its Culture lost,
rows.notes: TM had lowercase 'culture'; glossary term is 'Culture'.

rows.en: Vrlitwhai's forces covered the Macross as it drove on through space.
Along the way, it cut down Zentradi soldiers left bewildered by Minmay's song.
At last, the Macross closed in on the heart of the Main Fleet,
The only way for humanity to survive was to destroy the enemy's nerve center.
As the Macross launched its attack,
the Valkyries stormed into the mobile fortress.
The Main Fleet's commander and core unit of Boddole Zer's mobile fortress,
With its chain of command gone, the Main Fleet
no longer had the strength to attack the Macross.
And so the Space War, fierce beyond measure, came to an end.
Leaving behind the legend of Minmay's song...
The Galaxy Whale was struck by the poachers' reaction weapon.
But the whale shrugged off the reaction weapon as if it were nothing.
Seeing this, Basara began singing to the whale.
The Galaxy Whale responded to Basara's song and let out a cry.
Or rather, it began singing along with Basara's song.
Singing together with Basara, the Galaxy Whale
absorbed tremendous energy and shook the ground of Zola.
It held a power that overwhelmed all who witnessed it.
Eventually the whales vanished into the far reaches of the galaxy, still singing.
And so the session that seemed like it might never end
between Basara and the whales came to a close.
Thanks to the efforts of the Zolan Star Patrol, the poachers were swept away.
Satisfied after singing his heart out with the whales, Basara
left Zola behind and flew off to the far reaches of space.
Under a sudden Vajra attack, the Galaxy fleet sent out a distress signal.
But the Frontier government ignored the distress signal.
rows.notes: Frontier seifu = the Frontier government (glossary has only the 'Administrative Bureau' form, needs_research).

rows.en: Told by Grace that the Galaxy fleet was in danger, Sheryl
paid S.M.S. out of her own pocket to go to the Galaxy fleet's rescue.
rows.notes: Japanese: with her own pocket money she requested S.M.S. to rescue the Galaxy fleet. 'paid ... to go to the rescue' carries both.

rows.en: Taking the job, S.M.S. launched Mission "Galactic Fairy."
rows.notes: Japanese: 'In response to this request, mission "Galactic Fairy" was launched.' Made S.M.S. the subject of the active verb; mission name from lore 'Galactic Fairy' (episode/mission title not in glossary missions).

rows.en: In the cockpit of Alto's fighter, bound for the battlefield, Sheryl's earring glittered.
Meanwhile, on Island 1, Sheryl's revenge concert had begun.
rows.notes: 'revenge live' = Sheryl's revenge concert (the rematch of her interrupted concert).

rows.en: Realizing that Sheryl's song was meant for Alto and the others on the battlefield,
rows.notes: Sentence runs over 4148-4149; cut at the clause boundary (the Japanese cuts before 'realized').

rows.en: Ranka found herself joining in with a song of her own.
When the song crossed space-time and flowed from Alto's earring, an anomaly occurred.
Drawn by the singing, the Vajra had folded toward the Frontier fleet.
A swarm of Vajra bore down on Sheryl's concert venue.
The citizens of the Frontier fleet fled in panic.
And Ranka, who had made herself a decoy, was captured by the Vajra.
But Sheryl, whose concert had been cut short, began to sing again.
Ranka noticed, and she began to sing as well.
Reacting to Sheryl and Ranka's voices, the Vajra fell into confusion.
Seizing that opening, S.M.S. and the Battle Frontier attacked,
drove off the giant Vajra battleship, and the Vajra withdrew.
rows.notes: 'Vajra battleship' not in glossary as a unit name; translated literally (lowercase).

rows.en: And so the Frontier fleet repelled the Vajra attack.
On Island 1, snow began to fall, as if to announce the end of the battle.
Yet the damage from this battle was far from small.
And above all, the Vajra threat had not truly passed...
The U.N. Forces stood helpless before the crushing assault of Ingues's Mardook Army.
rows.notes: Ingues: glossary status 'wiki'. Mardook Army from the glossary alias.

rows.en: Silvie took Hibiki and slipped aboard the Macross.
With a surprise attack harnessing the Macross's runaway energy,
they aimed to turn the tables by taking down Ingues.
rows.notes: Subject restored as 'they' (Silvie and Hibiki, from 4165).

rows.en: The Macross rose up and fired its main cannon at Ingues's ship.
But even with the Macross's runaway energy behind it,
the attack had no effect at all on the Mardook Mothership.
Hibiki and Silvie despaired at that overwhelming power.
But Ishtar, who had secretly come aboard the Macross, did not give up.
Ishtar called out to the Mardook Army to stop fighting.
Her plea seemed about to reach the Emulators,
rows.notes: Sentence runs over 4174-4175. Emulator as in mission row u0370.

rows.en: but Ingues began punishing those who disobeyed him with death.
her heart full of feelings, sang a song of love.
And on hearing that song, Feff at last rose up against Ingues.
To protect the Mardook, and to protect Ishtar.
rows.notes: Deliberate fragment, kept as in the Japanese.

rows.en: Under a full barrage from the entire fleet, Ingues perished along with his ship.
The battle ended, and a peace treaty was signed between the Mardook and Earth.
With Earth's crisis over, Ishtar set off together with Feff and the others.
To build a culture for the Mardook, far out in space...
